claim: When a route serves executable code as a template literal with no build step, add a test that fetches the response and parses it (new Function / a parser), because the host language compiler checks the string as text and a backtick in a comment ships a syntax error to every consumer.
because: This round added a comment containing backticks inside the embed.js template literal; tsc and eslint were green, and only the new parse test (src/app/api/v1/widgets/embed.js/route.test.ts) went red before the commit.

claim: When deferring a provider to idle in a component tree, never let the deferred component become a NEW ANCESTOR of children that are already mounted — mount side-effect-only providers as siblings, and keep context providers in the tree from the first render with the heavy work deferred inside them — because a changed ancestor type remounts the entire subtree, so the deferral pays for its saving by tearing down and re-creating the very page it was protecting.
because: goat 885f4a9: the root shell rendered `ready ? <Prefetch><Palette>{children}</Palette></Prefetch> : children`; a jsdom mount counter showed the whole app body at mounts=2 / unmounts=1 one idle tick after first paint on every page (blank flash while the chunks loaded). Sibling shape: 1 / 0. The same shape in MatchProviders (mounts=2) cannot take the sibling fix because its provider carries React context — that is the second half of the rule. prefetch-and-defer covers fetch deferral and reapers but says nothing about tree identity.

claim: When a utility-first CSS engine reads theme keys by namespace (Tailwind v4 --font-*/--text-*), gate the theme by compiling it with the real engine over an inline candidate list and asserting each declared key emits a rule, because a key in a stale namespace compiles to nothing and no linter, type-checker or browser reports the absent class.
because: goat app-shell: --font-family-* and --font-size-* keys (v3 names) had emitted nothing since the v4 upgrade; font-grotesk (29 sites), font-mono (60) and text-2xs (210) were no-ops; a 100 ms @tailwindcss/node compile in vitest made it red-then-green (1bb7389).

claim: When a token file is @imported without layer() and its overrides live inside @layer blocks, the overrides can never win the cascade; assert one unlayered authority per token in a test over the compiled stylesheet, because the layered copy reads as the live value to every editor and is silently dead.
because: goat app-shell: 7 surface/border tokens had an unlayered :root in design-tokens.css and both a duplicate :root and a .dark override inside @layer base in globals.css; the compiled output proved the .dark palette never applied (1e574bf removed the duplicate; the override is a design decision on the deck).

claim: When a ratchet holds both an unused-FILES bucket and an unused-EXPORTS bucket from the same dead-code scanner, importing an unreachable module from a new test moves that module's dead exports from the first bucket into the second, so the same debt reads as a RISE; either import the reachable authority the module re-exports, or expect and explain the bucket shift.
because: reduced-motion.test.ts importing micro-interactions.ts turned knip:unusedFiles -1 into knip:unusedExports +34 with no code change to that module; dropping the import (ccdc9bd) restored the buckets and the test still pins the copy that had diverged

claim: When one placement can be made by several input devices (mouse, keyboard, touch), route every path through one resolver that returns the stored record, and pin with a test that the written record is identical across paths, because the path added last is the one that synthesises a stand-in and the divergence is invisible at each site.
because: goat useQuickSelect fabricated a BacklogItem (category unknown, created_at now, no years) while useSwipeToRank resolved the real one; 5 fields differed per placed item depending on input device; fixed bcf6930 with a 3-test pin

claim: When an effect guards its writes with a mounted/alive ref that its cleanup disarms, re-arm the ref at the top of the effect body, because any dependency-driven restart otherwise runs the new session with the guard already off and the hook silently freezes on its last state.
because: useSupabaseAuth listed a caller callback in its deps; the restart disarmed mountedRef for good and SIGNED_IN after one re-render never reached state (test 0/1 -> 1/1 after re-arm + latch). effect-identity-and-latched-callbacks covers the callback and the teardown flag but not the one-way latch surviving restarts.

claim: When a local write is mirrored into a bounded queue (offline/sync), check the queue capacity BEFORE mutating the local copy, because a post-mutation check leaves the local tree and the queue disagreeing by one entry with no record that they diverged.
because: goat backlog-store addItemToGroup/removeItemFromGroup pushed the item, then found the 50-entry queue full and returned; a red-then-green test showed divergence 1 -> 0 after moving the guard (563f272)

claim: When a table's RLS is later widened to USING(true) by a migration, treat every route that mutates it as the sole authorization door and pin owner checks with a route test, because the database no longer refuses anything and the code that assumed it does stays silent.
because: blueprints: migration 20260315000002 replaced owner-scoped policies with USING(true); PATCH/DELETE/publish checked only is_system, so anonymous callers could rewrite or delete any community template — fixed in 96072d6 and 99fbdaf with tests that went red-then-green

claim: When a hand-maintained type file claims to mirror a database schema, pin the claim with a test that reads the DDL as ground truth and keeps two exception lists (typed-without-DDL, created-but-untyped) that are checked in BOTH directions, because a one-directional coverage list rots silently the day a gap closes.
because: goat src/types/database.ts claimed to mirror Supabase and to be regenerable; measured 11/19 tables typed and 5 typed with no DDL; the regeneration command would have deleted the file's own imports. A 100-line vitest over the SQL went red on a seeded CREATE TABLE and green on its removal (7b76f9e).

claim: When a user-stored colour or other free string is interpolated into an inline style on a page other users load, validate it to a closed grammar (#rgb/#rrggbb) at the paint site, because a style attribute accepts url() and a stored value becomes a beacon fetched by every viewer.
because: goat collections-manager: /api/collections stored `color` verbatim and 12 sites painted `${collection.color}20` into background/boxShadow on the public share page; fixed with one guard + a source-scan test (366457a).

claim: When a test must prove a component SETTLES, do not wrap the render in act(); count Profiler commits over a real-time window, because act() waits for effects to settle and turns a non-settling loop into a hang instead of a red.
because: CollectionToolbar looped at ~130 commits/s; the act()-based test hung past a 180 s runner timeout, the Profiler-window version went red (125 commits/1 s) then green (2-3) after the fix.

claim: When a migration adds a column to a table that a `SELECT *` view reads, re-create the view in the same step, because Postgres expands `*` at CREATE VIEW and the new column never reaches existing views
because: goat: top_groups was created 7 days before item_groups.item_count; /api/search selected item_count through the view and returned [] on the error until the view was re-created (1ddf8b2). Neither schema-drift-detection nor idempotent-steps names view expansion.

claim: When an upsert relies on ON CONFLICT over a unique key that includes a nullable column, treat NULL rows as unguarded and look up by natural key before inserting, because NULLs are distinct under a plain UNIQUE constraint and the conflict clause silently never fires.
because: seed-yearly-games.js re-runs inserted +630 items and +21 lists per run; a select-then-insert with IS NULL fixed it and a fake-client test pinned existing-row -> 0 writes (3cd8fec)

claim: When a ratchet counter reads a subprocess's diagnostics as data, accept a non-zero exit only if the output holds at least one line of the diagnostic shape; otherwise COULD NOT RUN, because a compiler that crashed prints no diagnostics and therefore reads as zero findings.
because: goat ratchet.mjs counted a stub tsc that died with heap-out-of-memory (exit 134) as 0 errors and reported every bucket matching; fixed in 634f5c7 and proven red-then-green with the stub.

claim: When a coverage gate enumerates areas, derive the population from the version-control index, never a directory walk, because an empty directory exists only on the machine that deleted its contents and makes the count machine-dependent.
because: goat doc-coupling.mjs read 72 unmapped areas on one checkout and 70 on a clean clone of the same commit after two dead-file deletions; fixed in 76e6711 with a test that creates an empty directory and asserts the count does not move.

claim: When a seed or migration script upserts with an ON CONFLICT target, pin that target to a UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY column set parsed from the committed schema files in a unit test, because a target no constraint covers makes Postgres refuse every batch and the script reports "saved 0" as if the data were the problem.
because: seed-categories.ts upserted item_groups on `slug` (no such column) and items on `name,group_id` (no constraint) - 0 rows ever written, undetected because scripts/ sat outside tsc and eslint and the script needs paid credentials to run; a 60-line test over db/*.sql caught both and a mutation (padStart) red-then-green proved the sibling fixture test bites

claim: When auditing reduced-motion coverage, enumerate SMIL <animate> elements inside inline SVG as their own engine and gate them at the component that owns the <svg>, because the app's hook- or CSS-based reduction never reaches SMIL and an illustration library can carry dozens of indefinite opacity pulses that no existing mechanism sees.
because: goat: 47 <animate repeatCount=indefinite> across two illustration modules ran under every motion tier while the framer surfaces beside them honoured it; a per-component allowAmbient read took the count to 0 under the reduced tier (ambient-loops.test.tsx, 30 red -> 31 green). The registry's reduced-motion-mechanics names the engine-scoped rule but lists stylesheet, library and scripted loops as the engines; SMIL is a fourth that inline-SVG-heavy React trees carry.

claim: When a sortable item is also a drop target, the payload its droppable half carries is its DRAG payload, so a drop parser must read the source fields (source.tierId / orderInTier) for that target kind, because a parser written against a separate drop-payload shape refuses every item-to-item drop while both readers look correct in isolation.
because: goat DragOperationRouter.parseTarget read data.tierId for tier-item targets; TierItem (useSortable) carries UnifiedDragData with source.tierId; every same-tier reorder onto a card was refused. Fixed in 0562913 with a red-then-green router test.

claim: When a fuzzy matcher short-circuits on substring containment, scale the score by the length ratio of the two strings, because an unscaled containment score makes every SHORT identifier match any longer one that happens to contain it -- at a confidence above the threshold that was tuned for whole-string similarity.
because: A 22-line word-overlap matcher returned 0.9 for ('Her','Hercules') and ('Up','Up in the Air'), over the 0.3 accept threshold of all four third-party fetchers that use it AND over the pipeline's 0.6 minConfidence, so short titles were routinely enriched from the wrong catalogue entry. Scaling by the length ratio took those to 0.34 and 0.14 while a genuine variant kept 0.67 via word overlap (498ff9e).

claim: When one type answers the same question at two scopes - an aggregate-everything method and its compute-one sibling - pin them to each other with a test that calls both on the same input and compares, because a divergence in which predicate each assumes reads correct in either method alone and is only visible in the pair.
because: FacetAggregator.aggregate() counted every facet under the full predicate while computeSingleFacet() on the same class lifted the facet's own selection; each method was internally consistent, both had been read by earlier sweeps, and the disagreement only surfaced when a test called both. The test that compares them is now the thing that stops it recurring.
